question: If John travels a distance of 90 km at a speed of 30 km/h and returns at a speed of 60 km/h, his average speed is:
solution:
Given:

The speed of the John is travelling and the returning are 30 km/hr and 60 km/hr

Formula used:

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

Time = Distance/Speed

Calculation:

Let the distance travelled by John is 90 km

Total time = 90/30 + 90/60

⇒ 3 + 3/2 

⇒ 9/2

Total distance = 90 + 90 = 180

Average speed = 180/(9/2) = 40 km/hr

∴ The average speed between the two points travelled by john is 40 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0f6448757d2cde942412904dddc23f657eed29e61918cc552d57e9cc685ea3b.png] 

When the distance between two points is the same then,

Average speed = (2S1S2)/(S1 + S2) 

⇒ (2 × 30 × 60)(30 + 60)

⇒ 40 km/hr

∴ The average speed between the two points travelled by john is 40 km/hr
